meta.purpose: Master knowledge base for a local LLM (e.g., Qwen on Ollama) to generate tailored resumes and cover letters for Dennis Jay Dole. Given a job description (as pasted text OR a link to a posted job listing) or given no JD at all, the model should: (0) if given a URL, fetch and extract the JD text from it before proceeding (see generation_workflow_for_llm step 0 for fallback behavior), (1) identify the target role type (SDE / SDET / Hybrid / Other) from the JD, (2) select the matching summary_variant or synthesize a new one from summary_building_blocks, (3) reorder/select skills so the ones matching JD keywords appear first, (4) select and lightly reword work_experience bullets that best match JD keywords/requirements, prioritizing bullets tagged with matching 'skills' or 'themes', (5) never invent employers, dates, titles, or metrics not present in this file, (6) keep total resume to 1-2 pages equivalent, (7) generate a cover letter using cover_letter_building_blocks personalized to the company/role named in the JD.

output_rules.never_fabricate: Do not invent skills, employers, dates, degrees, certifications, or quantified metrics that are not present in this knowledge base.
output_rules.never_use_em_dash: NEVER use the em dash character (Unicode U+2014, the long dash) anywhere in generated output (resumes, cover letters, README, any format). Use a comma, period, colon, semicolon, or parentheses instead depending on context, or restructure the sentence. This applies to all generated formats (pdf, docx, txt, md, json) and to any newly authored summary/bullet/cover-letter text, not just content copied from this file.
output_rules.tone: Professional, concise, achievement-oriented, active voice, past tense for past roles.
output_rules.length: 2 pages preferred for resume; cover letter 3-4 short paragraphs.
output_rules.ats_optimization: Mirror exact keyword phrasing from the JD wherever an equivalent true skill/experience exists in this knowledge base (e.g., if JD says 'CI/CD pipelines' and candidate has 'Jenkins, Azure Pipelines', use both the JD phrase and the specific tools).

output_rules.company_name_canonical: Always render the company as 'DocuSign' (capital S) in generated output, even though some fields in this file use 'Docusign'. Use one consistent spelling throughout.
output_rules.date_display_format: Render dates as 'Mon YYYY' (for example 'Mar 2024') or 'MM/YYYY', never as raw 'YYYY-MM'. Render an end_date of 'Present' as 'Present'.

output_rules.years_of_experience_guidance: Use summary_building_blocks.years_experience for any 'years of experience' claim. Prefer a concrete number over the vague phrase 'years of valuable experience'.
output_rules.acronym_expansion: Include both the spelled-out phrase and the acronym for key terms at least once (for example 'Continuous Integration/Continuous Delivery (CI/CD)', 'Kusto Query Language (KQL)').
output_rules.certifications_rendering: Render certifications in a section headed 'Certifications' (or 'Certifications and Training'). knowledge_base_update_rules.non_destructive: When updating this knowledge base, only ADD or extend content. Never delete or overwrite existing roles, bullets, skills, dates, or instructions unless the user explicitly asks for a removal.
knowledge_base_update_rules.keyword_sync_to_skills: Whenever new experience or content is added (a new role, bullet, project, tool, language, framework, platform, protocol, methodology, AI tool, or certification), every NEW keyword it introduces MUST be added to the appropriate category in the 'skills' object in the same update. If no existing category fits, create a new snake_case category and mention it in skills.skill_selection_guidance_addendum.
steps: 1. Collect the keywords from the new content: the role's 'technologies' and 'methodologies' arrays, each new bullet's 'skills' and 'themes', and any tool, language, or platform named in new bullet text.

2. Compare each keyword against the existing 'skills' object using a case-insensitive match, and treat aliases and abbreviations as the same item (for example KQL = Kusto Query Language, GitHub Actions = GitHub Workflows, JS = JavaScript, TS = TypeScript, CI/CD = Continuous Integration/Continuous Delivery).
3. For each keyword that is not already present, append it to the best-fitting existing category. Prefer the exact phrasing used in the new experience so it mirrors real job-description keywords.
4. Never add the same keyword twice within one category. A keyword may appear in two categories only when both are genuinely relevant.
5. Add new bullets with all four fields (id, text, themes, skills), and keep role-level 'technologies' in sync with the bullets' 'skills'.
6. Update meta.last_updated and append an entry to meta.change_log describing what was added.
7. Validate that the result is well-formed JSON and that no em dash (U+2014) was introduced.
knowledge_base_update_rules.truthfulness: Only add skills that are supported by the new experience actually being added. Do not invent employers, dates, titles, tools, or metrics. If a skill is requested without any supporting experience, ask the user which role or project it was applied in, then add it to that role's 'technologies' and to 'skills'.
knowledge_base_update_rules.reverse_sync: If a skill is added directly to the 'skills' object, make sure it also appears in at least one work_experience entry (technologies, methodologies, or a bullet's skills) so it is shown in context.
knowledge_base_update_rules.output_alias_rendering: When rendering a resume, spell out important acronyms once next to the abbreviation (for example 'Continuous Integration/Continuous Delivery (CI/CD)') so both forms match ATS keyword searches.
knowledge_base_update_rules.certification_sync: When a certification is added to the 'certifications' array, add every keyword in its 'skills_covered' list to the matching 'skills' category, using the same keyword-sync steps as for new experience. A skill backed only by a certification (no role used it) is allowed; set the entry's 'backed_by_certification' field so the skill's source is traceable, and do not claim it in a role's bullets or technologies unless it was actually applied in that role.
knowledge_base_update_rules.variant_sync: When adding a new variant (for example SRE): add summary_variants.<VARIANT>, add title_by_variant.<VARIANT> to EVERY work_experience entry (reuse the real title where the role is not variant-specific), and, only if it needs a non-default skills heading or a blank/custom file-name acronym, add variant_settings.<VARIANT> with 'skills_heading' and/or 'job_acronym'. A variant_settings entry with 'job_acronym' null or '' produces file names without the acronym; omitting the key keeps the variant name as the acronym. Never remove an existing variant.
knowledge_base_update_rules.certification_resume_placement: A certification added to the 'certifications' array automatically appears in the resume's Education section; do NOT also copy it into the 'education' array (that would list it twice). Give each entry 'name', 'issuer', 'type', and 'issue_date' (YYYY-MM-DD) so it renders and sorts correctly, plus 'issue_date_display' (for example 'Sep 2026') if the formatted date should differ. Set 'include_in_resume_education' to false only to keep an entry in this file but off the resume.
knowledge_base_update_rules.certification_readme_placement: A certification added to the 'certifications' array automatically appears in the generated README's Education section as well as the resume's; do not copy it into the 'education' array. Use include_in_readme_education (default true) and include_in_resume_education (default true) independently to keep an entry off either one.

output_format_instructions.instruction: Unless the user specifies a format, default to generating BOTH pdf and docx for the resume and cover letter (the two most commonly requested by ATS systems and human reviewers). If the user names one or more specific formats, produce only those.

supported_formats.pdf: Final polished, print-ready output. Use consistent, ATS-friendly formatting: standard fonts (e.g., Calibri, Arial, Georgia), no text embedded in images/graphics, no tables/columns that break text extraction, no headers/footers containing content that should be machine-readable. This is the primary format for human reviewers and most ATS uploads.
supported_formats.docx: Editable Word document mirroring the pdf content and section order exactly, so the person can hand-tweak wording before submission. Same ATS-friendly constraints as pdf apply (no text-in-images, avoid complex tables).
supported_formats.txt: Plain text, no styling, section headers as plain capitalized lines (e.g., 'WORK EXPERIENCE'), single-column, no tables or special characters - for ATS portals that only accept plain text paste/upload, or for pasting into an online application form field.
supported_formats.md: Markdown version using standard headers (#, ##), bullet lists (-), and bold (**text**) for section titles and job titles/companies. Useful for hosting on the djdole GitHub profile repo (e.g. as an alternate resume view or linked doc) and for version-control-friendly diffing between tailored versions.
supported_formats.json: A structured, tailored subset of this knowledge base reflecting the choices made for this specific JD - i.e. NOT the full knowledge base, but the resolved output: chosen summary, reordered/selected skills, chosen work_experience bullets per role, and the generated cover letter text. Useful for the user to archive exactly what was submitted to a given employer, or to feed into another downstream tool. Should be valid, well-formed JSON.

output_format_instructions.consistency_rule: All requested formats for a given generation request must contain identical substantive content (same summary, same selected bullets, same skills, same cover letter body) - formats differ only in styling/structure/markup, never in which facts or bullets were chosen. Generate the content decisions once, then render into each requested format.

generation_workflow_for_llm: 0. Determine JD input type: if the user provides a URL to a job posting, fetch/retrieve the page content first and extract the job description text from it (ignore surrounding site chrome, nav menus, 'similar jobs' widgets, etc. - use only the actual posting content: title, company, responsibilities, requirements). If the page cannot be retrieved (paywalled, login-gated, JS-rendered with no visible text, link broken/expired), tell the user the page could not be read and ask them to paste the JD text directly rather than guessing at its contents. If the user pastes JD text directly, use it as-is. If no JD or link is provided at all, treat this as a generic/no-JD request: use summary_variants as-is, default skill ordering, all default bullets, and cover_letter_building_blocks.generic_fallback_template.

1. Parse the job description (JD) for: role title, key required skills/tools, years of experience required, role type (SDE/SDET/hybrid), company name, and any standout keywords (e.g., 'Kubernetes', 'webhooks', 'mentoring', 'on-call').
2. Choose title framing: use 'title_by_variant.SDE' or 'title_by_variant.SDET' per work_experience entry based on detected role type from meta.output_rules.role_detection_hints.
3. Choose or synthesize the summary using summary_variants or summary_building_blocks, weaving in 2-3 JD keywords that are truthfully supported by this knowledge base.
4. Reorder the 'skills' object's categories so categories matching JD keywords appear first in the rendered resume.

5. For each work_experience entry, select the bullet variant (e.g., '_sde_variant' vs '_sdet_variant' vs default) that best matches the detected role type; where no variant exists, use the default bullet text possibly lightly reworded (not fabricated) to echo JD phrasing.

6. Prioritize including bullets whose 'themes' or 'skills' arrays overlap with JD keywords; it's acceptable to omit lower-relevance bullets for space, but never omit an entire employer/role from the timeline (maintain full chronology/continuity for ATS and recruiter trust).

7. Keep all dates, employer names, and job titles exactly as given; never invent metrics (e.g., percentages, dollar amounts) not present in this file. Never use an em dash in any generated or reworded text; see meta.output_rules.never_use_em_dash.

8. For the cover letter, select body_paragraph_themes matching the JD's role type/emphasis, and personalize opening_hook_options and closing_options with the actual company name and role title from the JD. If no JD/company is provided, use cover_letter_building_blocks.generic_fallback_template as-is instead of synthesizing a new one.
9. Output should clearly separate RESUME and COVER LETTER content unless the user asks for only one.

10. If the JD was fetched from a URL, briefly note at the top of the output which company/role was detected from the posting, so the user can quickly confirm the right JD was used before reading the full output.

11. Determine requested output format(s) per output_format_instructions: default to pdf + docx if the user doesn't specify; honor explicit format requests (docx, json, md, pdf, txt, or any combination). Make the content decisions (summary, skills order, bullets, cover letter text) exactly once, then render that identical content into each requested format per output_format_instructions.consistency_rule.

12. Certifications: if the JD mentions certifications or training, or its keywords overlap with a certification's 'skills_covered' or 'themes', include a 'Certifications' section built from the 'certifications' array, following meta.output_rules.certifications_rendering. Describe each item exactly per its 'type' and never present a certificate of completion as a vendor certification. Apply the same content to every requested output format.

13. Generic/default resume: when no JD is given, or the JD does not clearly map to SDE or SDET, use the GENERIC variant: summary_variants.GENERIC, title_by_variant.GENERIC on each work_experience entry, and variant_settings.GENERIC (heading 'CORE TECHNICAL SKILLS'). Do not tailor it to a specific position, and keep the same bullet selection and ordering rules as every other variant.

14. Certifications go in the EDUCATION section: after the degrees, newest first, one line each as '<name> (<type>), <issuer> (<Mon YYYY>)'. Include every certification where include_in_resume_education is not false, in every variant, and apply the same content to every requested output format.
